title: Furthest Building You Can Reach
prompt:
You are given an integer array `heights` representing the heights of buildings, numbered from 0. You start at building 0 and move to the next building in order. Moving from building `i` to building `i+1` costs nothing if `heights[i] >= heights[i+1]`. Otherwise, you must use either a ladder or bricks: `heights[i+1] - heights[i]` bricks, or one ladder (which can cover any height difference regardless of size).

Given `bricks` and `ladders`, return the furthest building index (0-indexed) you can reach if you use the bricks and ladders optimally.

examples.explanation: The uphill climbs are 5 (building1->2), 3 (building3->4), and 5 (building4->5). Use the ladder on one climb of 5 and bricks (3+5=8, more than the 5 available) would fail for both remaining climbs, so bricks cover the climb of 3 (2 bricks left) but not the second climb of 5, leaving you stuck after reaching building 4.

hints: Since ladders cover any climb for free, they're most valuable saved for the largest climbs — but you don't know in advance which climbs will be the largest.
Use bricks for every climb as you go, but keep a min-heap of the climb sizes you've paid bricks for so far.

Whenever the number of climbs you've paid for exceeds the number of ladders available, refund the smallest brick payment made so far by converting it (conceptually) to have used a ladder there instead — this always leaves you with the most bricks possible for future climbs. Stop as soon as bricks go negative.

solution.approach: Walk through the buildings, and for every uphill climb, tentatively pay for it with bricks and push the climb size onto a min-heap. Whenever the heap size exceeds the number of ladders, that means more climbs have been brick-paid than there are ladders to cover, so refund the cheapest brick payment (the heap minimum) back into the bricks pool — effectively retroactively deciding a ladder was used there instead, since ladders are best reserved for the largest climbs. If bricks ever goes negative, the furthest reachable building is the one before the current climb.
